message.content:
Below are two ways you can launch a **Compute Engine** instance that has an NVIDIA GPU (the closest match to an RTX A6000 that’s currently offered by Google Cloud is the **Tesla A100**) and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important**  
> *Google Cloud does **not** use the “EC2” terminology – that’s Amazon Web Services. In GCP the service is called **Compute Engine**.*  
> *If you truly need an RTX A6000, you’ll have to check whether your region supports that exact GPU type. As of now, the A100 is the only GPU that matches the performance tier of an RTX A6000.*

---

## 1️⃣ gcloud CLI Command

```bash
# Replace PROJECT_ID and ZONE with your own values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-b"

gcloud config set project "$PROJECT_ID"

gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000-instance \
    --zone "$ZONE" \
    --machine-type n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
    --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \         # Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
    --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \   # 1 A100 GPU
    --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \        # VM will be terminated on host maintenance
    --restart-on-failure                      # Auto‑restarts after failures
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu Cloud image repository. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds a GPU. `type=nvidia-tesla-a100` is the closest to an RTX A6000. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Determines what happens during host maintenance. `TERMINATE` is typical for GPU workloads. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Enables automatic restarts if the VM crashes. |

> 📌 **Tip** – If you need more vCPUs or memory, pick a larger machine type (e.g., `n1-highmem-16`). Just make sure the GPU type you choose is supported in the zone you’re launching into.

---

## 2️⃣ REST API Call (JSON)

If you prefer to use the raw Compute Engine REST API, here’s a minimal POST request you can send to the `instances.insert` endpoint.

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000-instance",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "maintenancePolicy": "TERMINATE",
  "restartOnFailure": true
}
```

### How to use it

1. **Get an OAuth 2.0 token** – Use `gcloud auth print-access-token` or any other method to obtain a bearer token that authorizes the request.  
2. **Replace placeholders** – Substitute `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your actual project ID and zone.  
3. **Send the request** – You can use `curl`, Postman, or any HTTP client library in your preferred language.

---

## 3️⃣ Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Verify that the zone you’re using supports the GPU type (`nvidia-tesla-a100`). |
| ✅ | Ensure you have the **Compute Engine API** enabled in your project. |
| ✅ | Check that you have enough quota for GPUs in that zone. |
| ✅ | If you need persistent storage beyond the boot disk, add additional `disks` entries. |
| ✅ | Consider setting a **preemptible** flag (`--preemptible`) if cost is a concern and your workload can tolerate interruptions. |

---

### Final Note

If you absolutely need an **RTX A6000** and it’s not listed among the available GPU types in your region, you’ll have to contact Google Cloud support or wait until they add that specific GPU to the Compute Engine catalog. Until then, the **Tesla A100** is the best match in terms of performance and is widely available across many zones.
